ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An open electrical circuit contains a wire loop in the shape of a semi-circle, that contains a resistor of resistance $R=0.2 \Omega$. The circuit is completed by a conducting pendulum in the form of a uniform rod with length $\ell=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $m=0.05 \mathrm{~kg}$, has no resistance, and stays in contact with the other wires at all times. All electrical components are oriented in the $y z$ plane, and gravity acts in the $z$ direction. A constant magnetic field of strength $B=2 \mathrm{~T}$ is applied in the $+x$ direction.
<image_1>

Ignoring self inductance and assuming that $\alpha \ll 1$, the general equation of motion is in the form of $\theta(t)=A(t) \cos (\omega t+\varphi)$, where $A(t) \geq 0$. Find $\omega^{2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit in the figure is located in a semicircular wire region within the plane of the paper; above there is a section of fixed wire and a resistor R connected in series; a conducting rod of length ℓ is connected like a pendulum at the black dot above, and maintains contact with the semicircular wire below. The dashed vertical direction indicates the small-angle equilibrium reference direction, and the angle between the rod and this direction is labeled α. The uniformly distributed dotted circles in the figure indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the paper outward, i.e. the +x direction; the arrow on the right shows gravity g downward. Reasoning: When the conducting rod rotates with angular velocity θdot, the linear velocity at distance r from the pivot is r θdot, and the infinitesimal motional electromotive force produced in the perpendicular magnetic field B integrates to ε = ∫_0^ℓ B r θdot dr = (1/2)Bℓ^2 θdot. The rod has no resistance, and the total resistance of the circuit is R, so I = ε/R = Bℓ^2 θdot/(2R). The current-carrying rod is subjected to an Ampere force in the magnetic field, and the magnitude of its magnetic damping torque about the pivot is ∫_0^ℓ r I B dr = I B ℓ^2/2 = B^2ℓ^4 θdot/(4R), with direction opposing the motion, therefore τ_B = -B^2ℓ^4 θdot/(4R). The restoring torque of gravity on the center of mass of the uniform rod is τ_g = -mg(ℓ/2)sinθ ≈ -mgℓθ/2. The moment of inertia of a uniform rod about an endpoint is I_p = mℓ^2/3, therefore the equation of motion is (mℓ^2/3)θddot + (B^2ℓ^4/(4R))θdot + (mgℓ/2)θ = 0. Dividing by mℓ^2/3 gives θddot + a θdot + ω_0^2 θ = 0, where a = 3B^2ℓ^2/(4mR), ω_0^2 = 3g/(2ℓ). The angular frequency of the damped vibration form θ(t)=A(t)cos(ωt+φ) satisfies ω^2 = ω_0^2 - (a/2)^2. Substitute B=2 T, ℓ=0.1 m, m=0.05 kg, R=0.2 Ω: a = 3×2^2×0.1^2/(4×0.05×0.2)=3, therefore (a/2)^2=2.25. Take g≈9.8 m/s^2, ω_0^2=3×9.8/(2×0.1)=147, so ω^2=147-2.25=144.75≈145.

raw_record.question_text:
An open electrical circuit contains a wire loop in the shape of a semi-circle, that contains a resistor of resistance $R=0.2 \Omega$. The circuit is completed by a conducting pendulum in the form of a uniform rod with length $\ell=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $m=0.05 \mathrm{~kg}$, has no resistance, and stays in contact with the other wires at all times. All electrical components are oriented in the $y z$ plane, and gravity acts in the $z$ direction. A constant magnetic field of strength $B=2 \mathrm{~T}$ is applied in the $+x$ direction.

Ignoring self inductance and assuming that $\alpha \ll 1$, the general equation of motion is in the form of $\theta(t)=A(t) \cos (\omega t+\varphi)$, where $A(t) \geq 0$. Find $\omega^{2}$.

method.method_draft: Direct torque-and-current route. First read the diagram: the rod is a radius-like conducting pendulum in the yz plane, hinged/contacting at the upper black point and sliding on the semicircular wire; the dashed vertical is the small-angle reference, the resistor R is on the fixed top wire, magnetic-field dots indicate B along +x/out of the page, and gravity points downward. From the text take R=0.2 Ω, ℓ=0.1 m, m=0.05 kg, B=2 T, no rod resistance, and no self-inductance. For a rod rotating with angular speed θdot in a uniform perpendicular B field, compute the motional emf along the rod: ε=∫_0^ℓ B r θdot dr=(1/2)Bℓ^2 θdot, so I=ε/R. The magnetic torque on the current-carrying rod is opposing motion: τ_B=-∫_0^ℓ r I B dr=-(B^2ℓ^4/(4R))θdot. The gravitational torque about the pivot is τ_g= -mg(ℓ/2)sinθ≈-mgℓθ/2. With rod moment of inertia I_p=mℓ^2/3, form I_p θddot + (B^2ℓ^4/(4R))θdot + (mgℓ/2)θ=0. Divide by I_p to identify the damped oscillator coefficients: θddot+aθdot+ω_0^2θ=0, where a=3B^2ℓ^2/(4mR) and ω_0^2=3g/(2ℓ). The oscillation frequency in θ=A(t)cos(ωt+φ) is ω^2=ω_0^2-(a/2)^2. Substituting the numbers with g≈9.8 gives 147-2.25=144.75≈145.

method.method_draft: Energy and flux/Joule-dissipation route. First read the diagram: the moving rod sweeps area inside the semicircular circuit as it swings about the upper contact; its lower end stays on the circular arc, the resistor is the only resistance, field dots show uniform B perpendicular to the circuit plane, and the dashed vertical gives the equilibrium/small-angle line. From the text take R=0.2 Ω, ℓ=0.1 m, m=0.05 kg, B=2 T, and ignore self-inductance. Treat the rod as a physical pendulum with kinetic energy T=(1/2)(mℓ^2/3)θdot^2 and small-angle potential U=mg(ℓ/2)(1-cosθ)≈mgℓθ^2/4. The changing magnetic flux through the loop comes from the area swept by the radius-like rod: dA/dt=(1/2)ℓ^2 θdot, so ε=B dA/dt=(1/2)Bℓ^2 θdot. Since the resistor is the only dissipative element, Joule power is P=ε^2/R=(B^2ℓ^4/(4R))θdot^2. Use the energy balance d(T+U)/dt=-P; after differentiating and dividing by θdot, obtain (mℓ^2/3)θddot+(B^2ℓ^4/(4R))θdot+(mgℓ/2)θ=0. Then identify the damped sinusoid frequency as ω^2=3g/(2ℓ)-[3B^2ℓ^2/(8mR)]^2, which evaluates to about 145.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中电路位于纸面内，整体是一个半圆形导线回路，上方水平段中有电阻 R。均匀导体杆长度标为 ℓ，一端接触上方导线附近的铰接/接触点，另一端接触半圆弧，因此杆像半径一样扫过半圆内部区域。杆与竖直虚线之间的小角标为 α，虚线表示平衡位置。图中大量带点圆圈表示磁场垂直于电路平面，右侧箭头显示重力 g 向下。

推理：把导体杆看成绕上端接触点摆动的均匀物理摆。其转动惯量为 I = mℓ^2/3，所以动能 T = (1/2)(mℓ^2/3)θdot^2。小角度下，重力势能 U = mg(ℓ/2)(1 - cosθ) ≈ mgℓθ^2/4，因此回复力矩对应的线性刚度为 mgℓ/2。

杆转动时扫过的面积变化率为 dA/dt = (1/2)ℓ^2 θdot。磁通变化产生感应电动势 ε = B dA/dt = (1/2)Bℓ^2 θdot。电阻 R 是唯一耗能元件，所以焦耳热功率 P = ε^2/R = B^2ℓ^4 θdot^2/(4R)。

用能量方程 d(T+U)/dt = -P，得到
(mℓ^2/3)θddot + (B^2ℓ^4/(4R))θdot + (mgℓ/2)θ = 0。

除以 mℓ^2/3：
θddot + [3B^2ℓ^2/(4mR)]θdot + [3g/(2ℓ)]θ = 0。

阻尼振动角频率满足
ω^2 = 3g/(2ℓ) - [3B^2ℓ^2/(8mR)]^2。

代入 B = 2 T，ℓ = 0.1 m，m = 0.05 kg，R = 0.2 Ω，g ≈ 9.8 m/s^2：
3g/(2ℓ) = 147，
3B^2ℓ^2/(8mR) = 1.5，
ω^2 = 147 - 1.5^2 = 144.75 ≈ 145。

图像描述：图中电路位于纸面内，整体是一个半圆形导线回路，上方水平段中有电阻 R。均匀导体杆长度标为 ℓ，一端接触上方导线附近的铰接/接触点，另一端接触半圆弧，因此杆像半径一样扫过半圆内部区域。杆与竖直虚线之间的小角标为 α，虚线表示平衡位置。图中大量带点圆圈表示磁场垂直于电路平面，右侧箭头显示重力 g 向下。

推理：把导体杆看成绕上端接触点摆动的均匀物理摆。其转动惯量为 I = mℓ^2/3，所以动能 T = (1/2)(mℓ^2/3)θdot^2。小角度下，重力势能 U = mg(ℓ/2)(1 - cosθ) ≈ mgℓθ^2/4，因此回复力矩对应的线性刚度为 mgℓ/2。

杆转动时扫过的面积变化率为 dA/dt = (1/2)ℓ^2 θdot。磁通变化产生感应电动势 ε = B dA/dt = (1/2)Bℓ^2 θdot。电阻 R 是唯一耗能元件，所以焦耳热功率 P = ε^2/R = B^2ℓ^4 θdot^2/(4R)。

用能量方程 d(T+U)/dt = -P，得到
(mℓ^2/3)θddot + (B^2ℓ^4/(4R))θdot + (mgℓ/2)θ = 0。

除以 mℓ^2/3：
θddot + [3B^2ℓ^2/(4mR)]θdot + [3g/(2ℓ)]θ = 0。

阻尼振动角频率满足
ω^2 = 3g/(2ℓ) - [3B^2ℓ^2/(8mR)]^2。

代入 B = 2 T，ℓ = 0.1 m，m = 0.05 kg，R = 0.2 Ω，g ≈ 9.8 m/s^2：
3g/(2ℓ) = 147，
3B^2ℓ^2/(8mR) = 1.5，
ω^2 = 147 - 1.5^2 = 144.75 ≈ 145。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This route avoids calculating magnetic force or torque directly; it obtains the damping coefficient from flux-induced emf and Joule power via an energy balance.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to see that the rod sweeps a sector area in the semicircular loop, that B is perpendicular to the page/circuit, that the resistor is in the fixed loop, and that the small displacement is relative to the vertical dashed line.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text for component values and assumptions: R, ℓ, m, B, no self-inductance, zero rod resistance, and α≪1.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use Faraday’s law in the motional form ε=B dA/dt, Joule heating P=ε^2/R, rotational kinetic/potential energy of a uniform rod pendulum, and the standard underdamped oscillator relation for the observed cosine frequency.

raw_record.original_question:
An open electrical circuit contains a wire loop in the shape of a semi-circle, that contains a resistor of resistance $R=0.2 \Omega$. The circuit is completed by a conducting pendulum in the form of a uniform rod with length $\ell=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $m=0.05 \mathrm{~kg}$, has no resistance, and stays in contact with the other wires at all times. All electrical components are oriented in the $y z$ plane, and gravity acts in the $z$ direction. A constant magnetic field of strength $B=2 \mathrm{~T}$ is applied in the $+x$ direction.

Ignoring self inductance and assuming that $\alpha \ll 1$, the general equation of motion is in the form of $\theta(t)=A(t) \cos (\omega t+\varphi)$, where $A(t) \geq 0$. Find $\omega^{2}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: The circuit in the figure is located in a semicircular wire region within the plane of the paper; above there is a section of fixed wire and a resistor R connected in series; a conducting rod of length ℓ is connected like a pendulum at the black dot above, and maintains contact with the semicircular wire below. The dashed vertical direction indicates the small-angle equilibrium reference direction, and the angle between the rod and this direction is labeled α. The uniformly distributed dotted circles in the figure indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the paper outward, i.e. the +x direction; the arrow on the right shows gravity g downward. Reasoning: When the conducting rod rotates with angular velocity θdot, the linear velocity at distance r from the pivot is r θdot, and the infinitesimal motional electromotive force produced in the perpendicular magnetic field B integrates to ε = ∫_0^ℓ B r θdot dr = (1/2)Bℓ^2 θdot. The rod has no resistance, and the total resistance of the circuit is R, so I = ε/R = Bℓ^2 θdot/(2R). The current-carrying rod is subjected to an Ampere force in the magnetic field, and the magnitude of its magnetic damping torque about the pivot is ∫_0^ℓ r I B dr = I B ℓ^2/2 = B^2ℓ^4 θdot/(4R), with direction opposing the motion, therefore τ_B = -B^2ℓ^4 θdot/(4R). The restoring torque of gravity on the center of mass of the uniform rod is τ_g = -mg(ℓ/2)sinθ ≈ -mgℓθ/2. The moment of inertia of a uniform rod about an endpoint is I_p = mℓ^2/3, therefore the equation of motion is (mℓ^2/3)θddot + (B^2ℓ^4/(4R))θdot + (mgℓ/2)θ = 0. Dividing by mℓ^2/3 gives θddot + a θdot + ω_0^2 θ = 0, where a = 3B^2ℓ^2/(4mR), ω_0^2 = 3g/(2ℓ). The angular frequency of the damped vibration form θ(t)=A(t)cos(ωt+φ) satisfies ω^2 = ω_0^2 - (a/2)^2. Substitute B=2 T, ℓ=0.1 m, m=0.05 kg, R=0.2 Ω: a = 3×2^2×0.1^2/(4×0.05×0.2)=3, therefore (a/2)^2=2.25. Take g≈9.8 m/s^2, ω_0^2=3×9.8/(2×0.1)=147, so ω^2=147-2.25=144.75≈145.
